claim: A substantial fraction of the genome is transcribed in a cell-type-specific manner, producing long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), rather than protein-coding transcripts.
source: A substantial fraction of the genome is transcribed in a cell-type-specific manner, producing long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), rather than protein-coding transcripts.
evidence: This is a general statement about genome transcription that draws from established scientific knowledge about lncRNAs.

claim: The analysis of annotated and de novo assembled lncRNAs showed many are regulated during differentiation and mis-regulated in disease.
source: Our analysis of annotated and de novo assembled lncRNAs showed many are regulated during differentiation and mis-regulated in disease.
evidence: This claim is supported by the transcriptome analysis performed in the study.

claim: An in vivo RNAi screen in a model of acute myeloid leukemia identified several lncRNAs essential for leukemia maintenance.
source: We assessed lncRNA function via an in vivo RNAi screen in a model of acute myeloid leukemia. This identified several lncRNAs essential for leukemia maintenance
evidence: This is directly supported by the experimental screen results presented in the manuscript.

claim: A number of lncRNAs act by promoting leukemia stem cell signatures.
source: This identified several lncRNAs essential for leukemia maintenance, and found that a number act by promoting leukemia stem cell signatures.
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis and immunophenotyping data showing enrichment of leukemia stem cell signatures.

claim: Leukemia blasts show a myeloid differentiation phenotype when these lncRNAs were depleted.
source: Leukemia blasts show a myeloid differentiation phenotype when these lncRNAs were depleted
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing upregulation of CD11b and downregulation of c-Kit.

claim: The myeloid differentiation effect upon lncRNA depletion is mediated via effects on the MYC oncogene.
source: our data indicates that this effect is mediated via effects on the MYC oncogene.
evidence: This is supported by MYC rescue experiments showing that enforced MYC expression rescues the differentiation phenotype.

claim: A lncRNA expressed across all progenitors was required for the myeloid lineage.
source: Bone marrow reconstitutions showed that a lncRNA expressed across all progenitors was required for the myeloid lineage
evidence: This is supported by bone marrow transplantation experiments showing depletion of Pilna-expressing cells in the myeloid compartment.

claim: The leukemia-induced lncRNAs were dispensable in the normal setting.
source: whereas the other leukemia-induced lncRNAs were dispensable in the normal setting.
evidence: This is supported by bone marrow transplantation experiments showing no effect of Pvt1 and Lilam knockdown on normal hematopoiesis.

claim: lncRNAs have emerged as an additional layer of regulation of gene expression.
source: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as an additional layer of regulation of gene expression (Rinn and Chang, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: lncRNAs are defined as transcripts longer than 200 bp with little or no evidence of protein coding capacity.
source: Although their definition is rather arbitrary – transcripts longer than 200 bp with little or no evidence of protein coding capacity
evidence: This is a standard definition in the field based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: lncRNAs have essential and diverse reported functions.
source: their reported functions are essential and diverse (Wang and Chang, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: lncRNAs have been identified as important for dendritic cell specification, epidermal, and cardiac differentiation.
source: lncRNAs important for dendritic cell specification, epidermal, and cardiac differentiation have been identified (Grote et al., 2013; Klattenhoff et al., 2013; Kretz et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: lncRNAs are differentially expressed in human cancers.
source: Several recent large-scale cataloging efforts have highlighted how lncRNAs are also differentially expressed in human cancers (Du et al., 2013; Iyer et al., 2015; Yan et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: HOTAIR promotes metastasis in breast cancer through re-location of PRC2.
source: In breast cancer models, HOTAIR has been shown to promote metastasis through re-location of PRC2 (Gupta et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: PVT1 expression correlates with MYC protein levels and influences its stability.
source: PVT1 expression correlates with MYC protein levels and influences its stability (Tseng et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: LUNAR acts as an enhancer-like RNA, activating expression of IGF1R in T-ALL.
source: Amongst them, LUNAR was shown to act as an enhancer-like RNA, activating expression of IGF1R (Trimarchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: lncRNA-EPS promotes survival and inhibits apoptosis in murine fetal erythroblasts.
source: lncRNA-EPS promotes survival and inhibits apoptosis in murine fetal erythroblasts (Hu et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: lncRNA-EPS represses key immune genes in macrophages to restrain inflammation in vivo.
source: and represses key immune genes in macrophages to restrain inflammation in vivo (Atianand et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: lncRNA-DC is required for dendritic cell differentiation through its binding to STAT3.
source: In humans, lncRNA-DC is required for dendritic cell differentiation through its binding to STAT3 (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: GENCODE-annotated lncRNAs are regulated in mouse early hematopoietic progenitors.
source: Global analyses showed GENCODE-annotated lncRNAs to be regulated in mouse early hematopoietic progenitors (Cabezas-Wallscheid et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Two novel lncRNAs were characterized and found to regulate HSC function.
source: hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), where two novel lncRNAs were characterized and found to regulate HSC function (Luo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A comprehensive analysis of lncRNA dynamics through normal and malignant hematopoiesis has yet to be reported.
source: A comprehensive analysis of lncRNA dynamics through normal and malignant hematopoiesis has yet to be reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature at the time of the study.

claim: The murine hematopoietic system is a very well characterized model of stem and progenitor cell differentiation.
source: The murine hematopoietic system is a very well characterized model of stem and progenitor cell differentiation.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about the hematopoietic system.

claim: Many of the same transcription factors required for progenitor self renewal and specification are involved in malignant transformation.
source: Many of the same transcription factors required for progenitor self renewal and specification are involved in malignant transformation (Krivtsov et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: AML is often driven by fusion transcription factors or chromatin modifiers, such as MLL-AF9.
source: AML is often driven by fusion transcription factors or chromatin modifiers, such as MLL-AF9, that maintain an aberrant transcriptional landscape in transformed cells.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about AML.

claim: Interfering with chromatin-modifying complexes can lead to a substantial reduction in proliferation of AML cancer cells.
source: Consequently, interfering with these chromatin-modifying complexes can lead to a substantial reduction in proliferation of these cancer cells (Dawson et al., 2011; Roe et al., 2015; Shi et al., 2013; Zuber et al., 2011c).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: One of the reported functions for lncRNAs is the regulation of gene activity through interactions on chromatin.
source: Interestingly, one of the reported functions for lncRNAs is the regulation of gene activity through interactions on chromatin.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about lncRNA functions.

claim: HOTTIP activates expression of Hox genes by mediating recruitment of histone methyltransferase complex WDR5-MLL.
source: For example, lncRNAs HOTTIP and HoxBLinc, have been shown to activate expression of Hox genes by mediating recruitment of histone methyltransferase complexes WDR5-MLL and Setd1a/MLL1, respectively (Deng et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: HoxBLinc activates expression of Hox genes by mediating recruitment of histone methyltransferase complex Setd1a/MLL1.
source: For example, lncRNAs HOTTIP and HoxBLinc, have been shown to activate expression of Hox genes by mediating recruitment of histone methyltransferase complexes WDR5-MLL and Setd1a/MLL1, respectively (Deng et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: HOTAIR regulates the chromatin landscape via recruitment of PRC2 and the LSD1/CoREST/REST complexes.
source: and HOTAIR regulates the chromatin landscape via recruitment of PRC2 and the LSD1/CoREST/REST complexes (Rinn et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Deep RNA sequencing was performed using 11 cell types representing different stages of hematopoietic differentiation.
source: We performed deep RNA sequencing (RNAseq) using 11 cell types representing different stages of hematopoietic differentiation, ranging from long-term hematopoietic stem cells (LT-HSC) to differentiated cell types and blood cancers (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: Each library was sequenced and mapped to the mm10 genome assembly, with an average of 100 million uniquely mapped reads.
source: Each library was sequenced and mapped to the mm10 genome assembly, with an average of 100 million uniquely mapped reads.
evidence: This describes the sequencing depth achieved in the study.

claim: De novo transcriptome assembly was performed for each library using cufflinks.
source: We performed de novo transcriptome assembly for each library using cufflinks (Trapnell et al., 2010), with the GENCODE annotation (Harrow et al., 2006) as a reference transcriptome.
evidence: This describes the computational method used for transcriptome assembly.

claim: Over half of the lncRNAs assembled were unique to this study.
source: Interestingly, over half of the lncRNAs assembled were unique to our study, likely due to our sequencing depth and the number of new cell types included (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the overlap analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A meta analysis of transcriptional start sites within the full lncRNA catalog revealed a correlated open chromatin signal in every cell type with ATACseq data.
source: A meta analysis of transcriptional start sites (TSSs) within our full lncRNA catalog revealed a correlated open chromatin signal in every cell type with ATACseq data.
evidence: This is supported by the ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The number of lncRNAs in the catalog that showed enrichment varied between cell types.
source: The number of lncRNAs in our catalog that showed enrichment varied between cell types (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is supported by the ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: No signal above background was observed at the start of the second exon as a control region.
source: We performed the same analysis for the start of the second exon as a control region, and no signal above background was observed.
evidence: This describes a negative control analysis for the ATAC-seq signal.

claim: Assembled lncRNAs showed enrichment in ATACseq signal at their presumed TSS in at least one cell type irrespective of their relationship to surrounding protein-coding genes.
source: Irrespective of their relationship to surrounding protein-coding genes, our assembled lncRNAs showed enrichment in ATACseq signal at their presumed TSS in at least one cell type (Figure 1—figure supplement 1﻿).
evidence: This is supported by the ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: PCA based on the 500 most variable protein-coding genes showed that lymphoid differentiated cell types clustered together and separated from myeloid differentiated cell types and progenitors.
source: The lymphoid differentiated cell types CD3, PreB, and ProB clustered together and clearly separated from the myeloid differentiated cell type Gr1 and the progenitors.
evidence: This is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Oligopotent progenitors and long-term repopulating hematopoietic stem cells are found in close proximity in PCA, indicating that they share some transcriptional programs.
source: Despite having very different functional properties, oligopotent progenitors and long-term repopulating hematopoietic stem cells (LT-HSCs) are found in close proximity, indicating that they share some transcriptional programs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the PCA results shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The acute myeloid leukemia samples clustered closest to the granulocyte macrophage progenitor (GMP) population.
source: The acute myeloid leukemia samples, both in vivo (AML) and in vitro (RN2 cell line), clustered closest to the granulocyte macrophage progenitor (GMP) population, consistent with previous reports for this AML model (Krivtsov et al., 2006) (Figure 1E, left).
evidence: This is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 1E and a citation to prior literature.

claim: PCA based on lncRNA expression patterns replicated all the features observed with protein-coding genes.
source: PCA based on lncRNA rather than coding gene expression replicated all the aforementioned features, indicating that lncRNA expression patterns are overall very similar to those of coding genes (Figure 1E, right).
evidence: This is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The expression signatures from the study's data were in substantial agreement with prior microarray datasets with the exception of CLPs.
source: In general, our data was in substantial agreement with prior microarray datasets with the exception of those from CLPs.
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published microarray data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The staining strategy and isolation protocols for CLPs differed from those used in the previous report.
source: Notably, CLPs were the one cell type where our staining strategy and isolation protocols (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) differed from those used in the previous report.
evidence: This explains the discrepancy observed with CLP data.

claim: Expression module analysis identified differentially expressed lncRNAs and protein-coding genes that showed the same expression patterns.
source: We identified differentially expressed lncRNAs and protein-coding genes that showed the same expression patterns.
evidence: This describes the co-expression analysis performed in the study.

claim: The expression modules followed expected groupings, with enriched expression in either myeloid, lymphoid, or progenitor compartments.
source: The modules followed expected groupings, with enriched expression in either myeloid, lymphoid, or progenitor compartments.
evidence: This is supported by the expression module analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The MDS1 and EVI1 complex locus (Mecom) is known to regulate hematopoietic stem cell self-renewal.
source: Among the genes with enriched expression in LT-HSCs, we noted the MDS1 and EVI1 complex locus (Mecom). These are known to regulate hematopoietic stem cell self-renewal (Yuasa et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Hoxa9 and Meis1 are landmarks of MLL-AF9 AML self renewal.
source: Hoxa9 and Meis1, landmarks of MLL-AF9 AML self renewal (Krivtsov et al., 2006), are found in the module corresponding to genes enriched in both progenitors and our AML samples.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Rag1/2, Ebf1 and Cd38 are key regulators in lymphoid development.
source: Key regulators in lymphoid development such as Rag1/2, Ebf1 and Cd38 appear in the lymphoid-enriched module
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about lymphoid development.

claim: Csf3r and Itgam (CD11b) are in the module enriched for Gr1 expression.
source: while Csf3r and Itgam, also known as CD11b, part of the Mac-1 receptor, are in the module enriched for Gr1 expression (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the expression module analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Some level of correlation was detected between lncRNAs and their closest gene neighbors when examining expression levels across cell types.
source: When we examined expression levels across cell types between lncRNAs and their closest gene neighbors, we indeed detected some level of correlation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The correlation between lncRNAs and their closest genes was not exclusive to divergent transcripts.
source: However, this correlation was not exclusive to divergent transcripts, as a similar level of correlation was observed for other genomic organizations (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Enriched binding of transcription factors known to play a role in maintaining the transcriptional landscape of AML was observed around the TSS of lncRNAs in the catalog.
source: In the AML datasets, we observed enriched binding of transcription factors known to play a role in maintaining the transcriptional landscape of this model of leukemia (Roe et al., 2015) around the TSS of lncRNAs in our catalog (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and a citation to prior literature.

claim: lncRNA expression through development and disease is regulated by the same mechanisms as coding genes.
source: This suggests that lncRNA expression through development and disease is regulated by the same mechanisms as coding genes, hence leading to generally similar expression patterns.
evidence: This is an inference based on the transcription factor binding and expression correlation data.

claim: Differential expression analysis identified lncRNAs that were enriched in hematopoietic stem cells.
source: To explore this possibility, we performed differential expression analysis and identified lncRNAs that were enriched in hematopoietic stem cells, shared by the progenitor populations while showing lower expression in differentiated cell types, or enriched exclusively in the lymphoid compartment (Figure 3A, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Many lncRNAs with enriched expression in AML were identified.
source: We also noticed many lncRNAs with enriched expression in AML, as well as shared expression between AML and other cell types.
evidence: This is supported by the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The shERWOOD algorithm was used to predict highly potent shRNAs targeting each lncRNA candidate.
source: We used the shERWOOD algorithm (Knott et al., 2014) to predict highly potent shRNAs targeting each lncRNA candidate.
evidence: This describes the computational method used for shRNA design.

claim: A library containing at least four hairpins per lncRNA was designed, cloned and sequence verified into a doxycycline-inducible retroviral vector.
source: We designed, cloned and sequence verified a library containing at least four hairpins per lncRNA into a doxycycline-inducible retroviral vector.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for the screen.

claim: Virus production, infections and injections were performed using pools of 50 shRNAs.
source: To ensure a good representation of every hairpin during the 14 days that the cells proliferate in vivo, we performed virus production, infections and injections using pools of 50 shRNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the screen.

claim: Most shRNAs for Rpa3 were depleted by the final time point.
source: As expected, most shRNAs for Rpa3 were depleted by the final time point.
evidence: This is supported by the screen results shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Most hairpins targeting Renilla luciferase were not significantly changed during the 2-week time course.
source: Importantly, most hairpins targeting Renilla luciferase, which is not expressed in the MLL-AF9 leukemia cells and serves as a negative control, were not significantly changed during the 2-week time course.
evidence: This is supported by the screen results shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 20 primary hits were identified as potentially required for leukemia maintenance in vivo.
source: This produced a list of 20 primary hits that were potentially required for leukemia maintentenance in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the screen results shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 14 of the 20 lncRNA candidates showed a depletion of over 50% for both hairpins over the 14-day time course in competitive proliferation assays.
source: 14 of our 20 lncRNA candidates showed a depletion of over 50% for both hairpins over the 14-day time course, which represents a 70% validation rate of the initial hits (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by the validation assays shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Both primary and validated hits displayed a range of different expression levels.
source: Both our primary and validated hits displayed a range of different expression levels (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 9 out of 14 lncRNAs were selected for follow up experiments based on the severity of the proliferation phenotype and its consistency across independent knockdowns.
source: We selected 9 out of these 14 lncRNAs for follow up experiments based on the severity of the proliferation phenotype and its consistency across independent knockdowns (Figure 4E).
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for further analysis.

claim: For four of the selected lncRNAs, over 70% knockdown efficiency was observed in at least one of the clonal lines for both primers and both hairpins.
source: For four of our selected lncRNAs, we observed over 70% knockdown efficiency in at least one of the clonal lines for both primers and both hairpins.
evidence: This is supported by the qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Two lncRNAs had a more modest (~60%) but consistent knockdown across hairpins and primer pairs.
source: Additionally, two others had a more modest (~60%) but consistent knockdown across hairpins and primer pairs.
evidence: This is supported by the qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Most lncRNA knockdowns failed to induce any reproducible change of expression in either of their two flanking coding genes.
source: We did not observe any consistent trend, with most lncRNA knockdowns failing to induce any reproducible change of expression in either of their two flanking coding genes (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by the qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Knockdown of the two divergent lncRNAs, lncRNA_041249 and lncRNA_097790, did not cause any changes in the divergent coding transcripts, Srsf5 and Rmb27, respectively.
source: Knockdown of the two divergent lncRNAs, lncRNA_041249 and lncRNA_097790, did not cause any changes in the divergent coding transcripts, Srsf5 and Rmb27, respectively (corresponding to 'Upstream gene' in Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by the qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Depletion of lnc_166788 affects its closest neighboring gene Gata2.
source: The only case where we found depletion of a lncRNA to affect its closest neighboring gene was lnc_166788.
evidence: This is supported by the qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: lnc_166788 might be involved in promoting Gata2 expression and hence its depletion reduces Gata2 mRNA levels.
source: Our data indicate that this lncRNA might be involved in promoting Gata2 expression and hence its depletion reduces Gata2 mRNA levels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis showed an enrichment for Macrophage Differentiation genes upon knockdown of lnc_071255 (Pvt1), lnc_104449, or lnc_177417.
source: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) showed an enrichment for Macrophage Differentiation genes (Ingenuity Pathway Analysis list) upon knockdown of lnc_071255 (already annotated as Pvt1), lnc_104449, or lnc_177417
evidence: This is supported by the GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Leukemia stem cell signatures showed enrichment in the control knockdown.
source: while leukemia stem cell signatures (Krivtsov et al., 2006) showed enrichment in the control knockdown (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5B and a citation to prior literature.

claim: Depletion of lnc_071255 (Pvt1), lnc_104449, or lnc_177417 led to the upregulation of the myeloid differentiation cell surface marker CD11B and downregulation of the stem cell marker c-Kit.
source: Additionally, depletion of these same lncRNAs led to the upregulation of the myeloid differentiation cell surface marker CD11B (also known as Mac-1) and downregulation of the stem cell marker c-Kit, as shown by flow cytometry (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by the flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The phenotype upon lncRNA depletion resembles the phenotype observed upon withdrawal of the oncogenic MLL-AF9 fusion protein.
source: This resembles the phenotype observed upon withdrawal of the oncogenic MLL-AF9 fusion protein (Zuber et al., 2011b)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: None of the nine lncRNAs required for AML showed depletion in 4T1 breast cancer cells even after 14 days in culture.
source: While Rpa3 was required for proliferation of 4T1 cells in vitro, none of our lncRNAs showed depletion even after 14 days in culture (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by the competition assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The lncRNAs are not required for general cell or tumor survival and growth, but rather are specifically required for leukemia maintenance.
source: indicating that these lncRNAs are not required for general cell or tumor survival and growth, but rather are specifically required for leukemia maintenance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the 4T1 cell line data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: A strong reduction of Myc protein levels was observed upon lnc_071255/Pvt1, lnc_104449, or lnc_177417 knockdown.
source: Indeed, we observed a strong reduction of Myc protein levels upon lnc_071255/Pvt1, lnc_104449, or lnc_177417 knockdown.
evidence: This is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: The mRNA levels of Myc were not reduced in a comparable manner to the protein levels for lnc_071255/Pvt1 and lnc_104449 as compared to lnc_177417.
source: Intriguingly, the mRNA levels of Myc were not reduced in a comparable manner to the protein levels for the lnc_071255/Pvt1 and lnc_104449 as compared to lnc_177417.
evidence: This is supported by the qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: Pvt1 has been proposed to act by stabilizing MYC protein in human breast cancer.
source: lnc_071255, which corresponds to the previously annotated lncRNA Pvt1, was recently shown to correlate with MYC protein, but not Myc mRNA levels. In human breast cancer, Pvt1 has been proposed to act by stabilizing MYC protein (Tseng et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Knockdown of any of the lncRNAs that induced a myeloid differentiation phenotype resulted in a decrease in a Myc target gene-expression signature.
source: We also examined whether MYC target genes were affected by depletion of our lncRNA candidates using GSEA and found that knockdown of any of the lncRNAs that induced a myeloid differentiation phenotype resulted in a decrease in a Myc target gene-expression signature (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the GSEA analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of Myc rescued the proliferation phenotypes for Pvt1 and Lilam knockdown.
source: Expression of Myc rescued the proliferation phenotypes for Pvt1 and Lilam knockdown, as shown by a growth competition assay.
evidence: This is supported by the competition assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Myc expression rescued the differentiation phenotype observed upon knockdown for each of the three lncRNAs (Pvt1, Lilam, Pilna).
source: Both datasets were consistent with Myc expression rescuing the differentiation phenotype observed upon knockdown for each of these three lncRNAs (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the immunophenotyping and Giemsa staining data shown in Figure 6D-E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is an epistatic relationship between the lncRNAs (Pvt1, Lilam, Pilna) and Myc.
source: This strongly suggests an epistatic relationship between our lncRNAs and Myc and indicates that Pvt1, Lilam and Pilna exert their functions through Myc in this context.
evidence: This is an inference based on the MYC rescue experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Depletion of all five tested lncRNAs was observed in the MLL/ENL model.
source: We observe depletion of all five tested lncRNAs (Lilam, Pilna, Pvt1 plus two validated lncRNA hits with consistent knockdown) in the MLL/ENL model (similar to the MLL/AF9).
evidence: This is supported by the proliferation assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: A less striking phenotype was observed in a model where Myc is one of the drivers.
source: In a different model, where Myc is one of the drivers, we observed a less striking phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by the proliferation assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Enforced Myc expression rescues the phenotype of Lilam, Pilna and Pvt1 knockdown.
source: This is unsurprising since enforced Myc expression rescues the phenotype of Lilam, Pilna and Pvt1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the MYC rescue experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Chemical inhibition of Brd4, which leads to Myc downregulation, has little or no effect for mouse hematopoiesis.
source: However, previous studies have shown that chemical inhibition of Brd4, which also leads to Myc downregulation, has little or no effect for mouse hematopoiesis (Zuber et al., 2011c).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A significant depletion of zsGreen-expressing cells over time was observed with either hairpin targeting Pilna as compared to Renilla knockdown.
source: We observed a significant depletion of zsGreen-expressing cells over time with either hairpin targeting Pilna as compared to Renilla knockdown
evidence: This is supported by the bone marrow transplantation data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Little or no effect was observed for Pvt1 and Lilam shRNAs in bone marrow transplantation experiments.
source: while little or no effect was observed for Pvt1 and Lilam shRNAs (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by the bone marrow transplantation data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Both Pvt1 and Lilam were highly upregulated in leukemia cells (RN2) as compared to their most similar normal progenitors, GMPs, or HSCs.
source: When we examined the expression of these three lncRNAs, we observed that both Pvt1 and Lilam were highly upregulated in leukemia cells (RN2) as compared to their most similar normal progenitors, GMPs, or HSCs (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Pilna is broadly expressed across hematopoietic progenitors.
source: On the other hand, Pilna is broadly expressed across hematopoietic progenitors.
evidence: This is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Pilna has a more general role in hematopoiesis.
source: Our results suggest a more general role in hematopoiesis for Pilna
evidence: This is an inference based on the bone marrow transplantation and expression data shown in Figure 7.

claim: lncRNAs that show leukemia-enriched expression, Pvt1 and Lilam, could be dispensable for myeloid differentiation.
source: while lncRNAs that show leukemia-enriched expression, Pvt1 and Lilam, could be dispensable for myeloid differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the bone marrow transplantation and expression data shown in Figure 7.

claim: A correlation between lncRNA expression and that of the closest protein-coding gene was found.
source: We indeed find a correlation between lncRNA expression and that of the closest protein-coding gene
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The correlation in expression between lncRNAs and their closest genes arises from shared regulatory mechanisms or common regulatory environments.
source: We therefore hypothesize that this correlation in expression arises from shared regulatory mechanisms or common regulatory environments.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 20 lncRNAs whose expression confers a proliferative advantage to leukemia cells in vivo were identified by the shRNA screen.
source: By performing an shRNA screen targeting 120 lncRNAs, we identified 20 lncRNAs whose expression confers a proliferative advantage to leukemia cells in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the screen results shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Three lncRNAs emerged as candidates required for leukemia progression, as their depletion led to leukemic blast differentiation.
source: Three lncRNAs emerged as candidates required for leukemia progression, as their depletion led to leukemic blast differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by the GSEA and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Pvt1 is a marker of poor prognosis in colorectal cancer.
source: Amongst these was Pvt1, a lncRNA previously reported to be a marker of poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (Takahashi et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Pvt1 is required in MYC-driven cancers.
source: and shown to be required in MYC-driven cancers (Tseng et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The mechanism for human PVT1 function in breast cancer involves PVT1 stabilization of the MYC protein.
source: The mechanism for human PVT1 function, as shown in breast cancer, involves PVT1 stabilization of the MYC protein.
evidence: This is based on prior literature about PVT1 function.

claim: A similar effect of PVT1 on MYC protein levels is observed in the leukemia model.
source: We observe a similar effect in our leukemia model, with MYC protein levels being disproportionately reduced when PVT1 is depleted.
evidence: This is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: Pvt1, Lilam and Pilna have a direct or indirect functional relationship with Myc.
source: This suggests that these lncRNAs have a direct or indirect functional relationship with Myc, an oncogene upon which this AML model heavily depends.
evidence: This is an inference based on the MYC rescue experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Similar phenotypes have been shown when Myc levels are reduced by disturbing bromodomain containing 4 (Brd4).
source: This finding adds a layer to the already complex regulatory landscape of AML, and fits in with published results that have shown similar phenotypes when Myc levels are reduced by disturbing bromodomain containing 4 (Brd4) (Zuber et al., 2011c)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Similar phenotypes have been shown when Myc levels are reduced by disturbing the Myc superenhancer.
source: or the Myc superhancer (Shi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.
